edges.description: Demonstrates dominant neurotoxicity for one CMT2W allele, which is the property that separates a dominant-negative or gain-of-toxicity reading from simple haploinsufficiency.
edges.limitations: C. elegans has no myelinated peripheral nerve and no length-dependent axonal architecture comparable to a human limb nerve, so the model speaks to allele behaviour rather than to the neuropathy phenotype. Only one of the four reported alleles was tested this way.

edges.limitations: A developmental axon-outgrowth defect is not the same lesion as adult-onset, length-dependent degeneration of an established nerve, which is what CMT2W patients have. This is the specific translational gap the entry's HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion records.

evidence.reference_title: Histidine supplementation can escalate or rescue HARS deficiency in a Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease model.
evidence.snippet: In histidyl-tRNA synthetase (HARS), autosomal dominant mutations V133F, V155G, Y330C and S356N in the HARS catalytic domain cause Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 W (CMT2W), while tRNA-binding domain mutation Y454S causes recessive Usher syndrome type IIIB.

evidence.reference_title: Histidine supplementation can escalate or rescue HARS deficiency in a Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease model.
evidence.snippet: V133F proteins displayed reduced thermal stability in vitro, which was rescued by tRNA.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of function mutations in HARS cause a spectrum of inherited peripheral neuropathies.
evidence.snippet: All mutations cause a loss of function in yeast complementation assays, and p.Asp364Tyr is dominantly neurotoxic in a Caenorhabditis elegans model.

nodes.description: HARS1 is the cytoplasmic aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase that ligates histidine to its cognate tRNA. The CMT2W alleles — V133F, V155G, Y330C and S356N — all sit in the catalytic domain. Their consequences at the protein level are not uniform: V133F and Y330C reduce HARS1 abundance in cells and V133F is thermally destabilized in vitro (rescued by tRNA), while V155G and S356N retain enough activity to mischarge. This heterogeneity is the reason the downstream mechanism is curated as competing hypotheses rather than a single chain.

evidence.reference_title: Peripheral neuropathy and cognitive impairment associated with a novel monoallelic HARS variant.
evidence.snippet: Expression of this variant in patient cells resulted in reduced aminoacylation activity in extracts obtained from dermal fibroblasts, without compromising overall protein synthesis.

genetic_context.description: Heterozygous germline missense variants in the HARS1 catalytic domain. Modelling in neurons supports a dominant-negative rather than simple loss-of-function action; note that individual alleles also show reduced abundance, so the two are not mutually exclusive.

nodes.description: The cellular readout is failure of neuronal process formation and, in patients, degeneration of the longest peripheral axons. In neuronal cells the D364Y patient allele forms small HARS1 aggregates and inhibits process formation, whereas wild-type protein distributes through the cell body and supports normal differentiation. In patients this manifests as an axonal neuropathy; demyelination is not the primary lesion in CMT2 and is rarely seen early.

evidence.snippet: Type 2 CMT (CMT2) disease is a neuropathy with blunted or disrupted neuronal morphological differentiation phenotypes including process formation of peripheral neuronal axons.

nodes.description: Clinically the disorder is a Charcot-Marie-Tooth phenotype affecting sensory as well as motor nerves, with distal muscle weakness and wasting. Because the longest axons fail first, deficits begin distally in the feet and progress proximally. Onset can be late: one reported V133F patient presented at 49 years.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of function mutations in HARS cause a spectrum of inherited peripheral neuropathies.
evidence.snippet: Inherited peripheral neuropathies are a genetically heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by distal muscle weakness and sensory loss.

evidence.reference_title: Histidine supplementation can escalate or rescue HARS deficiency in a Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease model.
evidence.snippet: HARS is specifically associated with Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease type 2 W (CMT2W), an autosomal dominant axonal-form subtype of CMT. Most patients present with gait difficulties, foot deformities and distal sensory impairments (7).

nodes.description: The step between a partly defective synthetase and a dying axon is the least settled part of this disease, and the evidence supports more than one route. Neuronal models of dominant HARS1 alleles show increased eIF2-alpha phosphorylation with decreased protein translation, the integrated stress response signature. Separately, mischarging alleles produce insoluble protein accumulation, and at least one severe allele forms HARS1 protein aggregates directly. These are curated as competing hypotheses below; the node is marked PROVISIONAL because which route dominates in human peripheral nerve is unknown.
